2607.00482.title: Know When to Stop: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Reducing Overthinking
2607.00482.paper_summary: Reasoning language models frequently overthink: generating extended chains of behaviors such as hedging, approach abandonment, and self contradiction that consume tokens without improving answers. We show that these behaviors are not merely a consequence of length; even when controlling for response length, incorrect traces exhibit higher rates of unproductive self-reflection than correct ones. Addressing this requires identifying where self-reflection helps vs hurts, but obtaining these step-level annotations is costly. We observe that intermediate answer commitments within reasoning traces can provide a cheap proxy: by comparing each final answer candidate in the trace to the ground truth, we can determine whether subsequent reflection is productive without any additional supervision. Building on this insight, we propose DASH (Drift Aware advantage SHaping), which assigns segment-level credit based on whether each reasoning segment leads toward or away from correctness. On competition-level math benchmarks, DASH achieves the highest accuracy where overthinking is prevalent (AIME25: 50.8% vs. 45.4% GRPO) while reducing overthinking behaviors and achieving more productive self-correction than baselines.
2607.00482.paper_summary_zh: 推理語言模型經常過度思考：生成延長的行為鏈，如猶豫、放棄接近和自我矛盾，這些行為消耗了令牌卻未改善答案。我們顯示這些行為不僅僅是長度的結果；即使在控制回應長度的情況下，不正確的痕跡表現出比正確痕跡更高的無效自我反思率。解決這個問題需要識別自我反思在哪裡有幫助與有害，但獲得這些步驟級別的註釋是昂貴的。我們觀察到推理痕跡中的中間答案承諾可以提供一個廉價的代理：通過將痕跡中的每個最終答案候選與真實情況進行比較，我們可以確定後續的反思是否是有生產力的，而不需要任何額外的監督。在這一見解的基礎上，我們提出了DASH（漂移感知優勢塑造），它根據每個推理段落是否朝向或遠離正確性來分配段級別的信用。在競賽級數學基準測試中，DASH在過度思考普遍存在的情況下達到了最高的準確率（AIME25：50.8%對45.4% GRPO），同時減少了過度思考行為，並實現了比基準更具生產力的自我修正。
